slot.brief: A particle moves with a given position/velocity time function; compute the force as function of time and identify where the force changes direction.

stem: A bead of mass $3$ kg moves along the horizontal wire segment shown in the figure, with position $x=\left(\dfrac{t^3}{3}-2t^2+3t\right)$ m for $t\geq 0$. Which statement gives its force and when the force reverses direction?

verdicts.working: From x=t³/3−2t²+3t, a=d²x/dt²=2t−4. Thus F=ma=3(2t−4)=6t−12 N, which changes sign at t=2 s.
issues: The figure shows an electrical circuit, not a bead on a horizontal wire segment; it is unrelated to the stated motion.

working:
$v=\dfrac{dx}{dt}=t^2-4t+3$ m s$^{-1}$
$a=\dfrac{dv}{dt}=2t-4$ m s$^{-2}$
$F=ma=3(2t-4)=6t-12$ N
$F=0$ at $t=2$ s; its sign changes there.

Independent check: From x=t³/3−2t²+3t, a=d²x/dt²=2t−4. Thus F=ma=3(2t−4)=6t−12 N, which changes sign at t=2 s.
solution:
$a=\dfrac{d^2x}{dt^2}=2t-4\ \text{m s}^{-2}$, so $F=ma=3(2t-4)=6t-12\ \text{N}$.\\
$F=0$ at $t=2\ \text{s}$, and its sign changes there; hence the force reverses direction at $t=2\ \text{s}$.
